questions.q: When does a record get its Salesforce ID?
options: It is only assigned once the record is deployed to production
Salesforce generates and assigns it automatically the instant the record is created
IDs are optional and can be left blank
A user manually assigns it when creating the record
questions.explain: Every record gets a unique, system-generated ID automatically on creation — it isn't a field a user fills in, and it never changes afterward.

questions.q: What do the first three characters of a Salesforce ID identify?
options: The org's instance (which data center it's hosted in)
The record's creation date
The record's object type (its key prefix), consistent across every Salesforce org
The user who created the record
questions.explain: The key prefix — the first three characters — identifies the object type, such as 001 for Account or 003 for Contact, the same way in every org.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a 15-character and an 18-character Salesforce ID?
options: There is no difference — they are interchangeable in every context
The 18-character form is only used for custom objects
They refer to completely different records
The 15-character form is case-sensitive; the 18-character form encodes case and is case-insensitive
questions.explain: The 18-character ID adds three characters that encode the case of the original 15, making it safe to use anywhere case might get altered, unlike the case-sensitive 15-character form.

questions.q: A spreadsheet tool auto-capitalizes text, and an integration using 15-character IDs from that spreadsheet starts failing to match records. What is the most likely cause?
options: The object's key prefix changed
The spreadsheet's auto-capitalization altered the case-sensitive 15-character IDs, pointing them at the wrong records or none at all
15-character IDs cannot be used in integrations under any circumstances
The records were deleted
questions.explain: Because the 15-character ID is case-sensitive, any tool that silently changes capitalization can corrupt it; the 18-character form avoids this exact problem.

questions.q: Underneath the UI, what does a Lookup or Master-Detail relationship field actually store?
options: The related record's page layout
A formula that recalculates the relationship on every page load
A copy of the entire related record
A Salesforce ID pointing to the related record
questions.explain: Every relationship field covered in this chapter — Lookup, Master-Detail, junction — stores a Salesforce ID referencing the related record, not a copy of the record itself.
